title: Why the Nazca lines were drawn
summary: Scholars differ on the purpose of the Nazca lines, though most see religious meaning. Working out how they were made has been easier than knowing why.
why: Giant lines and figures cover a desert, and no one knows for sure why they were made.
question: Why did the Nazca people draw giant lines and figures across the desert?
evidence: Made roughly 500 BCE to 500 CE across Paracas and Nazca phases; some lines appear to follow aquifers; constellation links disputed by Aveni.
wouldSettle: Excavated offerings and dated activity along the lines showing how people used them.

theories.name: Astronomical markers
theories.idea: Kosok and Reiche proposed sighting lines for solstice sunrises and sunsets.

theories.name: Water and fertility ritual
theories.idea: Reinhard linked the lines to worship of water deities; some follow underground water.

theories.name: Ceremonial pathways
theories.idea: Lines served as walked ritual routes, irrigation tracks and calendar sites.
